name: Very Light Green
lede: Very Light Green is the modifier "very light" applied to [[green]], filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 and again by the xkcd crowd survey in 2010.

sections.title: A pale modifier on green
sections.body:
The name is built from the modifier "very light" plus the base color [[green]], not a separate coined word [1]. Our library places it in the ISCC-NBS dictionary's 1955 block 148, and it was recorded again, independently, in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey [1][2]. The library also lists two near-duplicate names at the same hex, "Very Pale Green" (0.4 units off) and "Washed Out Green" (2.2 units off) [1].

Its nearest look-alikes are [[tea-green]] (4.8 units, duller and darker), [[light-grey-green]] (6.4, darker) and [[celery]] (6.6, more vivid) [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color across at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed; that describes the limits of our archive, not the color itself [4].
